intro.title: useDeferredValue
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple search input component that filters a list of items in real-time. You will learn how to use Angular's `defer` block to optimize performance by deferring the rendering of computationally expensive updates until the browser is idle. The core concept involves delaying non-critical UI updates to keep the main thread responsive, preventing jank during user interactions. You will work with Angular templates, control flow, and the `@defer` syntax to implement this pattern. By the end, you'll understand how to improve user experience in data-heavy applications by prioritizing urgent updates over less critical ones.
intro.usecase: In real-world Angular applications, deferred values are crucial for optimizing performance in search interfaces and data-heavy dashboards. For example, when users type in a search box with live results, you can defer the expensive filtering operation while keeping the UI responsive to keystrokes. This pattern is commonly used in e-commerce product filters, admin panels with complex data visualizations, and analytics dashboards with real-time updates. By deferring non-critical updates, you prevent the UI from freezing during intensive computations, creating a smoother user experience.
